parties: Sanjay Gupta (acquirer/disclosing party); AVG Logistics Limited (target)
headline: Sanjay Gupta files SEBI Takeover Regulation 31(4) disclosure for substantial acquisition in AVG Logistics Limited
sum: Sanjay Gupta has filed a mandatory disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulation 31(4) signalling a substantial acquisition of shares in AVG Logistics Limited, triggering the public disclosure regime for shareholding acquisitions above prescribed thresholds.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure marks the point at which an acquirer's holding crosses material thresholds (typically 5%, 10%, 15%, 25% or 50%) and must be immediately disclosed to stock exchanges; this filing indicates the transaction is public but does not confirm completion, open offer obligation, or final shareholding % without access to the full disclosure document.
detail: Under SEBI (SAST) Regulations 2011, Regulation 31(4) requires any person whose shareholding in a listed company reaches or exceeds specified thresholds to file a disclosure with the stock exchange within 2 trading days. Sanjay Gupta's filing with NSE indicates a substantial acquisition event in AVG Logistics Limited. The precise threshold crossed, consideration amount, and acquisition structure (direct purchase, open offer, or derivative transaction) cannot be confirmed without the underlying PDF disclosure document, which appears to be archived at NSE.

framework.note: Mandatory disclosure by acquirer when shareholding reaches/exceeds 5%, 10%, 15%, 25%, 50% or 75% thresholds; must be filed within 2 trading days of acquisition.
Applicability: applies to listed companies (public companies); regulates persons acquiring substantial shares.
Acquisition via market purchase, open market, or negotiated basis; disclosure triggered upon actual holding.
Underlying statute empowering SEBI to regulate substantial acquisitions and takeovers.
Exemptions to disclosure: acquisition by persons acting in concert, off-market acquisitions below thresholds (where applicable).
Stock exchange rules require disclosure of material events; substantial shareholding crossing regulatory thresholds is material.
Open offer obligation triggered if acquisition crosses 25% of voting capital or if acquirer already holds 25% and acquires additional 5% in a 12-month period.

approvals: Disclosure to NSE and BSE within 2 trading days of acquisition

Material event disclosure requirement to stock exchange.
